'''David Leslie Andrews''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|FRSC}}, {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|FInstP}} (born 15 October 1952) is a British emeritus professor of [[Chemical Physics]] at the [[University of East Anglia]], where he was the Head of Chemical Sciences and Physics from 1996 to 1999.<ref name="profile">{{Cite web |title=David Andrews |url=https://research-portal.uea.ac.uk/en/persons/david-andrews |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=University of East Anglia |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Education ==
David Andrews graduated (1st Class Hons) in Chemistry from [[University College London]] in 1973. He then obtained a PhD in theoretical chemistry from the same university in 1976.

==Career==
In 1979, he joined the [[University of East Anglia]] as a Lecturer.<ref name="profile">{{Cite web |title=David Andrews |url=https://research-portal.uea.ac.uk/en/persons/david-andrews |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=University of East Anglia |language=en-GB}}</ref> Andrews was promoted to Senior Lecturer in 1991 and to Reader in 1994. He was appointed Professor of Chemical Physics in 1996<ref name="profile" /> and became Emeritus Professor in 2023.<ref name="A1">{{Cite web |title=Emeritus professor awarded prestigious Institute of Physics award |url=https://www.uea.ac.uk/about/news/article/emeritus-professor-awarded-prestigious-institute-of-physics-award |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250513125303/https://www.uea.ac.uk/about/news/article/emeritus-professor-awarded-prestigious-institute-of-physics-award |archive-date=2025-05-13 |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=University of East Anglia |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Andrews and his research group have published on the theory of [[Optics|optical phenomena]], developing [[Quantum electrodynamics|quantum electrodynamical theory]]<ref name="refC">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.3390/physics7040049  | doi-access = free| title = Molecular Quantum Electrodynamics: Developments of Principle and Progress in Applications | journal=Physics | volume = 7 | article-number = 49 | year = 2025 | last1 = Andrews | first1 = D.L. | issue = 4 | url=https://www.mdpi.com/2624-8174/7/4/49 }}</ref> and [[Molecular symmetry|symmetry principles]] for applications including [[fluorescence]] and [[Optical tweezers|optical nanomanipulation]].<ref name="refD1">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.72.033816 | title = Optically induced forces and torques: Interactions between nanoparticles in a laser beam | journal=Physical Review A| volume = 72 | article-number = 033816 | year = 2005 | last1 = Bradshaw | first1 = D.S. | last2 = Andrews | first2 = D.L. | issue = 3 | bibcode = 2005PhRvA..72c3816B | url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.72.033816 }}</ref> Andrews has worked on the quantum theory of [[Förster resonance energy transfer|intermolecular energy transfer]], including a theory of energy transfer that accommodates both radiationless and radiative processes.<ref name="refE1">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/0301-0104(89)87019-3 | title = A unified theory of radiative and radiationless molecular energy transfer | journal=Chemical Physics| volume = 135 |  pages = 195–201 | year = 1989 | last1 = Andrews | first1 = D.L. | issue = 2 | bibcode = 1989CP....135..195A | url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0301010489870193| url-access = subscription }}</ref> He has also contributed to [[quantum optics]] and [[nonlinear optics]], with studies of chiral interactions including a prediction of the [[Hyper Rayleigh Scattering Optical Activity|hyper–Rayleigh scattering]] effect.<ref name="ref10">
{{cite journal | doi=10.1063/1.437535 | title=Hyper−Raman scattering by chiral molecules | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics| volume=70 | page=1027 | year=1979 | last1=Andrews | first1=D.L. | last2=Thirunamachandran | first2=T.| issue=2 | bibcode=1979JChPh..70.1027A | url=https://ueaeprints.uea.ac.uk/id/eprint/56440/1/013.pdf}}</ref><ref name="C1">{{Cite web |title=2023 Thomas Young Medal and Prize {{!}} Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/2023-thomas-young-medal-and-prize |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=www.iop.org |language=en}}</ref> Research on [[Chirality (chemistry)|chirality]] and [[Circular dichroism|optical helicity]]<ref name="refF1">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.85.063810 | title = Chirality and angular momentum in optical radiation | journal=Physical Review A| volume = 85 | article-number = 063810 | year = 2012 | last1 = Coles | first1 = M.M. | last2 = Andrews | first2 = D.L. | issue = 6 | arxiv = 1203.1755 | bibcode = 2012PhRvA..85f3810C | s2cid = 118571061 | url=https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.85.063810 }}</ref> have led to contributions to the theory of [[Optical vortex|optical vortices]].

==Awards and recognition==
*2023: Thomas Young Medal and Prize<ref name="C1">{{Cite web |title=2023 Thomas Young Medal and Prize {{!}} Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/2023-thomas-young-medal-and-prize |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=www.iop.org |language=en}}</ref>
*2022: Faraday Division Horizon Prize<ref name="B1">{{Cite web |last=Royal Society of Chemistry |date=2021-06-07 |title=Chiroptical Harmony - 2022 Faraday Division Horizon Prize winner |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/2022-winners/chiroptical-harmony/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425063652/https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/2022-winners/chiroptical-harmony/ |archive-date=2025-04-25 |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en}}</ref>
*2021: President of [[SPIE]]<ref name="D1">{{Cite web |title=David Andrews elected to SPIE presidential chain |url=https://optics.org/news/9/8/40 |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=optics.org}}</ref>
*2016: Elected [[The Optical Society|Fellow of The Optical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Fellows {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/elected_fellows/2016_fellows/ |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>
*2005: Elected [[SPIE|Fellow of SPIE]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=David L. Andrews profile |url=https://spie.org/profile/David.Andrews-27665?SSO=1 |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=spie.org}}</ref>
*1999: Elected [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]]
*1988: Elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]]
